event: Instrumental opening
direction: Hold the plaza wide. Before the first vocal at 13.08, separation has to register through the distance between two figures.

event: You’ve broken heart; should’ve got a warning; it don’t have it, it just starts
direction: With the first vocal, move close enough to read her shoulders. Bare feet and their reflection make the walk feel exposed even while her face stays guarded.

event: A thousand promises; tearing you apart
direction: Let the divided reflections carry the fracture. When the level backs off, the image can still feel less stable than the previous phrase.

event: And you can get through the bitter cold; nobody’s perfect; no one’s sinless
direction: The lyric offers endurance before she feels relief. A body bracing against the wind can carry that pressure across a longer shot.

event: You are more than you ever know
direction: Let the raised eyeline reach its destination before the world changes. The circular opening in the city gives the eclipse a shape to inherit.

event: Open the window; pour in the light
drive: First release after the pre-chorus crest
direction: The music pushes outward as the first chorus answers the verse. Start the dancers already traveling and let the wider stage supply the release.

event: Leaving the shadows; oh, you got the power
direction: Find intimacy inside the chorus. A change of shot size makes the affirmation personal while the musical pulse continues.

event: Above and beyond; soar in the darkness
direction: Give the crossing or floorwork phrase enough width for the feet and landing to read. Expand travel at the same tempo.

event: Stronger than ever; find the answers; you got the power
direction: Let one dancer complete the line before the other answers. Shared direction carries the affirmation without requiring another location change.

event: Instrumental turnaround / held release
drive: Brief held release before the sustained phrase
direction: The vocal gap can sustain a balance or turn. Keep a small movement alive through the frame where the next phrase takes over.

event: Above and beyond — sustained beyond
drive: Long exhale; do not cut across the held word
direction: The held “beyond” lasts 6.70 seconds. Compare the planned long exhale with the moving v04 partner exchange and the dissolve into the city.

event: You’re not defeated; you will never be; you just haven’t won yet
drive: The setback is acknowledged, not resolved
direction: The return to the city acknowledges a setback. Carry a line of gold from the stage into the window geometry so the new pressure has a visual cause.

event: When you’re exhausted; feel like you’ve been haunted; remember who you haven’t met
direction: Let exhaustion accumulate in posture and gaze at the glass. A pause after traveling can read as an effort to keep going.

event: Don’t close your eyes; don’t hide your face; this heartache is temporary
drive: She turns to face the pain and chooses to continue
direction: Make the decision visible in the turn toward the open corridor. Keep room in the frame for her to choose her own direction.

event: Your greatest love is still out there
direction: Use the widening horizon to open a possible future. Let that suggestion land before the next traveling phrase takes over.

event: Open the window; pour in the light
drive: The release returns with greater certainty
direction: Return to the eclipse with both bodies already pushing across the floor. The second release has more certainty than their first entrance.

event: Leaving the shadows; you got the power
direction: Change level as well as camera angle. In the paired edit the floor sweep answers the crossing run and gives momentum a destination.

event: Above and beyond; stronger than ever; find the answers
drive: The pair move from parallel paths into alignment
direction: Let the second dancer answer the first across the frame. A reply in the same space makes their paths feel connected.

event: You got the power; oh, you got the power
direction: One look or an unbroken stride can carry the repeated affirmation. The v04 face-on walk offers a quieter counterpoint to the preceding travel.

event: Ooh, can you feel it?
drive: The tone turns intimate and reassuring
direction: Bring the question down to the scale of a face. Leave room for the response in the next phrase.

event: You’re not alone; ooh, can you feel it?
direction: “You’re not alone” answers the distance established in the plaza. A close-up can carry that answer; the forehead reserve is an optional insert.

event: You’re not alone; oh, can you feel it?
direction: Hold the shared direction long enough to let reassurance settle. A repeated line can deepen an action already underway.

event: Oh, can you feel it? Ooh, can you feel it?
direction: The arrangement grows while the emotional question feels more settled. Keep the horizon stable as the dancers change their relationship to it.

event: Ooh, can you feel it? Above and…
drive: The refrain lifts into the final build
direction: The highest archived cue-average level occurs here. Keep the phrase beginning at 2:43.36 continuous across the next cue boundary.

event: …and beyond; open the window; pour in the light
direction: Let the last syllable finish before demanding a second visual accent. Open the bodies into the final refrain while preserving the direction of travel.

event: Oh, you got the power
direction: In the edit, the run starts ahead of this cue. Judge its push-off against fixed floor seams, then watch the bodies diminish in the distance.

event: Above and beyond; soar in the darkness; stronger than ever
direction: Allow the traveling action to complete. This late lift is a confident extension, with less unresolved pressure than the bridge.

event: You’ll find the answers; you got the power
drive: The final affirmation resolves the movement
direction: Bring attention back to contact with the floor. When the camera widens, check the stage behind the dancers as carefully as the feet.

event: Above and beyond
drive: First repeated ending; begin to release intensity
direction: The first ending repeats the title. Reduce the number of new visual ideas so the audience can feel the repetition.

event: Above and beyond
direction: Stay with the two figures and let the field lose emphasis. The next walking shot can inherit their shared direction.

event: Above and beyond; instrumental tail to 3:33.456
direction: The last timed word ends at 3:26.40. Keep walking through the remaining music, with steadily smaller figures and a fixed horizon.
